-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in freshwater marshes, and other wetland areas.

## Natural history notes

A small wetland sparrow characterized by warm brown upperparts, gray face and breast, rusty wings, a reddish-brown cap, and dark streaking on the back. In Florida, it is mostly a winter visitor found in freshwater marshes, wet prairies, pond edges, ditches, sedge meadows, and other dense low vegetation near water. It feeds mainly on seeds and small insects, usually foraging low in grasses, reeds, and wet ground cover while staying hidden in thick vegetation.
